A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BoPITO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original data-generation, sample-efficiency and interpolation experiments on the Prinz potential and Alanine Dipeptide, with additional empirical analyses in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains original BoPITO evaluations and adds Chignolin experiments and molecular-system hyperparameter analyses.

M1.justification: V2 adds a system-specific score adaptation used for Chignolin: a lag-dependent multiplier on the equilibrium score and a capped lag input to the dynamic component beyond N_decay (A.7, Equations 22–24). The original BoPITO formulation, training objective and interpolator remain.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates a one-dimensional potential and a 22-atom peptide. V2 adds folding dynamics of the 10-residue Chignolin protein, using 93 heavy-atom coordinates from explicit-solvent simulations and a foldedness observable, substantially extending molecular complexity and task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 5 replaces the unbiased ITO comparator in v1 with an unbiased Markov state model in v2, while retaining biased ITO. The principal ITO-versus-BoPITO and BG-versus-crystal comparisons remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds Chignolin-specific settings, including native-contact correlations, 35,000-frame trajectories and a 30,000-step maximum lag. For retained Prinz experiments, the reported decay parameter becomes 0.994 throughout, replacing 0.982 for 1, 5 and 10 trajectories; this does not establish rerunning. The score-decay diagnostic also changes to an absolute-value average.

E4.justification: V1 already contains a Prinz decay-parameter sensitivity analysis. V2 extends this analysis to Alanine Dipeptide and Chignolin (Figure 8), including numerical training failures and identifying 0.9995 as the smallest stable tested Chignolin value.

E5.justification: V2 specifies four trained models per training-set size for Chignolin, using potentially overlapping random trajectory sets (A.9.2). The retained systems still use ten models, and the 95% confidence-band convention remains. This adds a distinct repetition count without establishing increased repetition of earlier experiments.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds Chignolin results showing lower long-time correlation errors for BoPITO than ITO. V2 also adds sensitivity and foldedness results (Figures 8 and 13), revises Figure 5's conditional distributions and reference comparator, and changes Figure 4's first displayed fitted interpolation parameter from 1000 to 1050.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 changes the eigenvalue–relaxation relation from lambda_i = exp(-tau*kappa_i) to its absolute-value form. The score-decay quantity also gains an absolute value inside its expectation (v1 Equation 19; v2 Equation 20). The existing spectral-decomposition proof is retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim improved sample efficiency, asymptotically unbiased equilibrium statistics, and recovery of approximate dynamics through observable-constrained interpolation. Abstract edits and the conclusion's revised enumeration retain these contributions and their scope.

C2.justification: V2 explains Chignolin short-time failures through imbalance between score components and numerical scales, motivating the adapted formulation (A.7). It also adds an explanation of interpolation's handling of out-of-distribution states (A.8) and interprets the expanded experiments as favorable scaling with system size.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link, four algorithms documenting training and sampling, and inference ODE step counts in Table 1. It also documents Chignolin preprocessing, training settings and request-based data access. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the pseudocode and newly disclosed inference counts alone do not establish procedural changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds Jing et al. on MDGen, Nicoli et al. on unbiased neural-sampler estimation, and Lindorff-Larsen et al. for Chignolin data. The existing related-work coverage and principal novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 3, parameter-fitting material moves earlier in the appendix, and definitions, explanatory passages, notation refinements and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from four panels to six, with methods arranged in rows and systems in columns; Figure 2 becomes vertically stacked beside text. V2 redraws Figure 5, adds Figures 8 and 13 and algorithm displays, and expands Table 1. Figure 3's caption incorrectly retains the previous orientation description.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical validation by testing protein-folding dynamics beyond the potential and small peptide, while documenting the necessary adaptation and numerical stability limits. Added pseudocode, inference details and code-access information also address important reproducibility gaps. These gains outweigh the limited presentation regression in Figure 3's mismatched caption.
